name: Pedestrian Safety Perception in Futian, Shenzhen (1–7 Rating)
description:
Method replication: same task, scale and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (106 Baidu street view panoramas re-fetched on a spread-out grid across Futian District, Shenzhen, 2017 or later, shown as the whole 360° view in one wide strip).

Original study: Huang, Lu, Cai & Han (2026), Buildings 16(5), 920. 1,000 Baidu panoramas were drawn across Futian with spatially stratified sampling. 30 local adult volunteers familiar with Futian rated pedestrian safety perception on a 1–7 Likert scale (higher = safer); each image was rated by three volunteers, so each volunteer rated about 100 images. The mean ratings trained a random forest model that predicted safety for the whole street network, analysed with MGWR.

Differences from the original study: (1) 106 new panoramas instead of 1,000; each participant rates 100 of them, so each image gets many more raters than three. (2) The question wording is ours; the paper only names the construct "pedestrian safety perception". (3) The car roof at the bottom of the panorama is cropped away. (4) A question on familiarity with Futian was added, because the paper recruited only local volunteers.
author: Huang, Lu, Cai & Han
